newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Cambodia ASEAN membership still on, Malaysia says.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia ASEAN membership still on, Malaysia says.

text.p: Despite teetering on the brink of civil war, Cambodia will join the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) as planned next month, Malaysia's Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.
"Our (ASEAN) position has not changed because the commitment has already been made," Anwar told reporters after a banking function.
The situation would be reviewed at ASEAN's annual meeting in Kuala Lumpur at the end of this month, he added.
"It is too early and premature to suggest anything, except immediate ceasefire," he said, when asked if ASEAN was proposing any solution to the problem.

Malaysia is the current chairman of ASEAN, which also groups Brunei, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. ASEAN decided on May 30 to induct Burma, Cambodia and Laos as the final members of the grouping.
"As it stands today, we will negotiate with both the PMs (prime ministers)," he said, when asked who ASEAN would negotiate with in Cambodia.
A long simmering rivalry between Cambodia's co-prime ministers, former communist party chief Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh, erupted into pitched fighting in the capital at the weekend.

Hun Sen has declared Ranariddh a traitor for negotiating with the reviled Khmer Rouge, in power during the "killing fields" regime of 1975-79. He has called for a new prime minister to be appointed by Ranariddh's royalist party.
Anwar said several messages had been sent to the two leaders through various channels.
"Our concern is peaceful resolution of the conflict," said Anwar, who is taking the place of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad while the latter is on an extended leave abroad.

The Cambodian capital Phnom Penh was quiet but tense as dawn broke on Monday but many residents feared a new round of fighting as forces loyal to the country's rival prime ministers faced off to the west of the city.
At least 12 people were killed and more than 50 wounded in a weekend of fighting on the streets of the capital.
All flights in and out of Phnom Penh were cancelled, leaving hundreds of foreigners stranded in the city since the weekend. Many of the stranded were in temporary accommodations.
Hun Sen's forces captured Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party headquarters and his home in heavy fighting on Sunday.
Thousands of Phnom Penh residents fled the city at the weekend by bus, truck and boat.
The two leaders have shared power in a coalition government set up after a 1993 election organised by the United Nations.
But they were opponents during a long civil war in the 1980s when Hun Sen was in power in Phnom Penh in a government backed by Vietnam.
